Harness web plugin that replaces the font settings in general settings with searchable font pickers.
# dsh-font-settings
English | 中文
A DeepSeek Harness web plugin that replaces the font settings in **Settings → General** with searcha
ble font pickers: text, code, and terminal fonts are set independently, and the fonts installed on y
our machine can be listed on request.
The shipped rows ask you to type a comma-separated font name from memory. This plugin shows you the
list instead — and draws every candidate in its own face, so you pick by sight.
## Features
- **Searchable pickers** for the text, code, and terminal font roles. Focus or type to open the list

; ↑/↓ move with wrap-around, Enter applies, Escape cancels the edit, a click outside closes it.
- **
Every row is drawn in the family it would apply**, so a candidate is recognized by how it looks rath

er than by its name.
- **Free text still works.** Anything not in the list can be typed; the harness

normalizes it (names are quoted, generic families stay bare) and it becomes the field's value.
- **
Load the fonts installed on this machine** with one button (Chromium-based browsers expose the list
through `queryLocalFonts`; where it is unsupported or denied, the button says so and everything else
keeps working). The catalog is searchable rather than dumped: type part of a family name and its ma

tches are listed.
- **Font size for every role**, next to its font picker.
- **Collapsed by default*
* to a single "Font settings" row with a chevron disclosure, so the General list stays compact. The

current text font is summarised on the collapsed row.
- **The system default is always one click awa
y** — the first entry in every list clears the override.
## Install
The plugin installs as a profile bundle. Use the Web sidebar's **Plugins** page, or the `plugin_mana
ger` tool's `install_bundle` (it requires `danger-full-access`). The spec can be a git address, a lo
cal path, or a registry name:
- **From GitHub**: `https://github.com/yiqiuacc/dsh-font-settings.git` (the manager runs `git ls-rem
ote` against GitHub before installing; pnpm's `github:yiqiuacc/dsh-font-settings` shorthand works to

o).
- **From a local checkout**: `link:<absolute path to this directory>`.
- **From a registry** onc
e published: `@styiqiu/dsh-font-settings`.
Installing enables the bundle by default. Opening **Settings → General** then shows one "Font settin
gs" row where the built-in font group used to be.
## Where the choice is stored
The plugin owns no storage and no stylesheet. Every read and write goes through the harness theme se
rvice (`ctx.theme`), so the shipped machinery does the rest:
- **Persistence** — the settings scope stores each list and size; the profile records them as the `u

i-theme` config row of its `cordis.patch.yml`.
- **First paint** — the harness boot script embeds th
e stored lists into the served index HTML, so a page never flashes the default font before applying

yours.
- **Application** — the theme presenter writes `--dsh-font-family-<role>` onto `body` as inli
ne styles, and the token sheet composes the interface and code stacks from them.
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
- `client.js` is the whole plugin. It registers one entry in the General section's item slot **using
the built-in entry's id at a lower priority**, which shadows that entry: a list slot renders one ro
w per id and the lowest priority wins. The group replaces the built-in font rows rather than sitting

beside them.
- The field and the candidate card are the shared client primitives — `Input`, `MenuSu
rface`, and `MenuGroup` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`, a client baseline module — so
the shared field geometry, menu material, sticky group headings, and focus behavior come from the ha

rness rather than from this plugin.
- The committed list is adopted as the field's text only while t
he field does not hold the keyboard, so a write landing while you type — including the echo of your

own commit — cannot replace what you typed or move the caret.
- The `theme` service is taken through
a scoped injection (`ctx.inject(['theme'], …)`). Where that service is absent, the plugin registers
nothing at all: the built-in font settings keep their place and the plugin is simply inert. The out

er plugin never waits on the service, so a composition without it still boots.
- `index.js` is an **
empty mount shell** (`export function apply() {}`). A profile bundle needs a mountable Host plugin f
or the Loader row to exist, and the browser bundle is discovered from that live entry — but this plu

gin has no Host-side behavior left.
- No build step and no dependencies of its own: plain ES modules
, with React and the client primitives supplied by the client module loader.
## Compatibility

- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.x` web (and Desktop, which uses the same web profile template).
- The local-

font button needs a Chromium-based browser. Everything else is engine-neutral.
- `ctx.theme` is a **
pre-stable API**: the harness states that public APIs can change, so a harness upgrade may require u
pdating this plugin.
## Known limitations
- **The local catalog is listed only while filtering, and at most 24 rows of it.** Every row is pain
ted in the family it would apply, and a cold font cache loads one font face per distinct family — hu
ndreds of rows in one open stall the page for seconds. The curated list is unaffected; a filtered lo

cal list costs about what the curated one costs.
- **The group sits above "Appearance".** Shadowing
requires a lower slot priority, and a list slot sorts by priority, so the group renders first in the

General section. This cannot be avoided while replacing the built-in rows.
- **It depends on the bu
ilt-in entry id `font-size`.** If a future harness renames that entry, the shadow stops applying and
this group renders **beside** the built-in font rows instead of replacing them — duplicated control

s, no crash and no error.
- **The roles are independent.** There is no "also replace the monospace f

ont" switch: the code and terminal roles have their own pickers.
- **No separate preview block** — e

ach list row is already drawn in its own face.
- **No font-size formatting beyond the harness ranges
** (text 10–22, code 10–16, terminal 10–20 px); the steppers clamp to them.
